<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VI.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|153}}</noinclude>that taketh avvay the things that are thine, aske not againe. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}}† And according as you vvil that men doe to you, doe you also to them in like maner. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}}† And if you loue them that loue you, vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also loue those that loue them. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}}† And if ye doe good to them that doe you good: vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also doe this. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}}† And if ye lend to them of vvhom ye hope to receiue: vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also lend vnto sinners, for to receiue as much. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=35}}† But loue ye your enemies: doe good and {{sup|‖}} lend, hoping for nothing thereby, and your reward shal be much, and you shal be the sonnes of the Highest, because him self is beneficial vpon the vnkinde and the euil. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=36}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon the first Sunday after Pentecost.}}Be ye therfore merciful as also your father is merciful. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=37}}† Iudge not, & you shal not be iudged. condemne not, & you shal not be condemned. forgiue, and you shal be forgiuen. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=38}}† Giue, and there shal be giuen to you. good measure & pressed dovvne and shaken together and running ouer shal they giue into your bosome. For vvith the same measure that you do meate, it shal be measured to you againe.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=39}}† And he said to them a similitude also: Can the blinde leade the blinde? doe not both fal into the ditch? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=40}}† The disciple is not aboue his maister: but euery one shal be perfect, if he be as his maister. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=41}}† And vvhy seest thou the mote in thy brothers eie: but the beame that is in thine ovvne eie thou considerest not? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=42}}† Or hovv canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me cast out the mote out of thine eie: thy self not seeing the beame in thine ovvne eie? Hypocrite, cast first the beame out of thine ovvne eie: and then shalt thou see clerely to take forth the mote out of thy brothers eie.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=43}}† For there is no good tree that yeldeth euil fruites: nor euil tree, that yeldeth good fruite. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=44}}† For euery tree is knovven by his fruite. For neither doe they gather figges of thornes: neither of a bush doe they gather the grape. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=45}}† The good man of the good treasure of his hart bringeth forth good: and the euil man of the il treasure bringeth forth euil. for of the aboundance of the hart the mouth speaketh.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=46}}† And vvhy cal you me, Lord, Lord: and doe not the things vvhich I say? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=47}}† Euery one that commeth to me, and heareth my vvords, and doeth them: I vvil shevv you to vvhom he is like. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=48}}† He is like to a man {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He buildeth right & surely, that hath both faith and good workes: he buildeth on sand, that trusteth to his faith or reading or knowledge of the scripture, and doth not worke or liue accordingly.}}∷ building a house, that digged deepe, and laid the foundation vpon a rocke. And vvhen an inundation rose, the riuer bette against that<noinclude>{{rh||V|house,}}</noinclude>
